title: Azure Cosmos DB: Vector Search & Global Conversational State
description: Architect globally distributed conversational state and vector search using Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL API in .NET.

data.text: The Role of Cosmos DB in AI Architectures

Generative AI applications require a database that can handle semi-structured chat transcripts, fast point-reads for user sessions, global distribution for multi-region frontends, and native vector search. Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL delivers single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, SLA-backed 99.999% availability, and integrated vector indexing capabilities (DiskANN and IVFFlat), making it an ideal repository for agent memory and conversation state.
Partition Key Strategy for AI Chat Sessions

Choosing the wrong partition key in Cosmos DB causes 'hot partitions' that throttle throughput (HTTP 429). In conversational AI, partitioning by TenantId or UserId ensures that all chat messages for a user are grouped together, enabling fast query performance for recent message history while evenly distributing reads across physical partitions.
Integrated Vector Search in Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL

Cosmos DB NoSQL allows storing vector embeddings directly alongside document properties in the same JSON document, eliminating the need to maintain separate synchronizations between a relational database and an external vector engine.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Cosmos DB provides global low-latency storage for agent memory and session transcripts
Partition by TenantId or UserId to avoid hot partitions and guarantee point-read efficiency
Integrated vector search allows querying vectors and JSON metadata in a single SQL statement
Session consistency provides the optimal balance of read-your-own-writes accuracy and low RU cost
Use the Cosmos DB Change Feed to trigger event-driven background vector sync pipelines
data.takeaway: Azure Cosmos DB combines global scale with native vector search, providing a unified storage backbone for enterprise conversational state and long-term agent memory.
